gloss: to demote; to downgrade; to relegate

definitions.gloss: to demote; to downgrade; to relegate
definitions.explanation: To lower someone or something in rank, status, or grade. Used in workplace hierarchies, sports leagues, and classification systems.

examples.japanese: {部長|ぶちょう}から{課長|かちょう}に{降格|こうかく}された。
examples.english: He was demoted from department head to section chief.

examples.japanese: チームが{二部|にぶ}リーグに{降格|こうかく}した。
examples.english: The team was relegated to the second division.

examples.japanese: {成績|せいせき}{不振|ふしん}を{理由|りゆう}に{降格|こうかく}{処分|しょぶん}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: He received a demotion due to poor performance.

notes:
Used both transitively (to demote someone) and intransitively (to be demoted / to drop in rank). In sports, equivalent to English "relegation" when a team drops to a lower division.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {降格|こうかく}{処分|しょぶん}: demotion (as disciplinary action)
- {降格|こうかく}{人事|じんじ}: demotion in personnel decisions
- {二軍|にぐん}に{降格|こうかく}する: to be sent down to the minor league
- {降格|こうかく}{圏|けん}: relegation zone (in sports leagues)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {昇格|しょうかく}する: to be promoted in rank — the antonym of {降格|こうかく}, meaning to move up in status or division
- {左遷|させん}する: to be transferred to a lesser position — implies a sideways move to a less desirable post as a de facto punishment, while {降格|こうかく} is an explicit rank reduction
- {格下|かくさ}げする: to downgrade — more general, can apply to ratings, classifications, and evaluations, not just personnel
